chunks: From him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who entered into Umrah and forgot to shorten [his garments] until he entered into Hajj. He said: He seeks forgiveness of Allah, and there is no penalty upon him, and his Umrah is complete.

key_terms.أَهَلَّ: To enter into the state of ritual consecration (Ihram) for pilgrimage
key_terms.دَخَلَ فِي الْحَجِّ: Entered into the state of Hajj
key_terms.يُقَصِّرَ: To shorten or cut (specifically referring to cutting hair or garments in the context of Umrah rites)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets to cut their hair after Umrah before starting Hajj?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Istibsar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that forgetting to cut the hair (qasr) after Umrah does not invalidate the ritual, as the pilgrim merely seeks forgiveness (istighfar) rather than paying a penalty (dam). This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of leniency in cases of unintentional omission during the Hajj rites, distinguishing it from cases where the hair is cut before the full completion of Umrah rituals. It underscores the importance of intention and the validity of the Umrah even if a subsequent step is delayed or forgotten.
